newsitem.title: USA: Alabama House approves $3.7 billion school budget.
newsitem.headline: Alabama House approves $3.7 billion school budget.

text.p: The Alabama House of Representatives has approved a $3.7 billion education budget that does not raises taxes or teacher pay, state officials said Friday.

The fiscal 1998 proposal allocates $2.56 billion for elementary, middle and high schools, up from $2.42 billion this year. Universities and colleges would get $975.9 million, up from $967.9 million this year.

Gov. Fob James had recommended cutting higher education's share to $958 million and raising public education's share to $2.44 billion. The House plan also allocates $19 million that James had recommended holding in reserve against revenue shortfalls.
Additionally, the House plan shifts funding for $25.3 million of education-related programs to the general fund budget. The proposal now goes to the Senate.
